title: Expose a Service via NodePort and LoadBalancer
description: Make your nginx app accessible from outside the cluster.
problemStatement:
## 🎯 Goal
Convert the existing Service to NodePort and then try LoadBalancer (if your cluster supports it, e.g., minikube tunnel).

### Steps
1. Use `kubectl edit svc nginx-svc` and change `type` to `NodePort`. Save and exit.
2. Check the assigned NodePort: `kubectl get svc nginx-svc` (look at PORT(S) column, e.g., 80:30080/TCP).
3. Find the node IP:
   - minikube: `minikube ip`
   - kind: `kubectl get nodes -o wide`
4. Access via curl or browser: `http://<node-ip>:<node-port>`. You should see nginx.
5. (Optional) If using minikube, you can also run `minikube service nginx-svc --url` to get the URL.
6. Now change the Service type to `LoadBalancer`. If on minikube, open a new terminal and run `minikube tunnel` (this simulates a cloud LB).
7. Check `kubectl get svc nginx-svc`. An EXTERNAL-IP should appear.
8. Access via that external IP: `curl http://<external-ip>`.
9. Revert back to ClusterIP or delete the Service when done.
hints: If using kind, LoadBalancer won't work without MetalLB; NodePort still works.
The `minikube tunnel` command must keep running; it creates a network route to the LoadBalancer IP.
NodePort range can be customized in kube-apiserver, but stick to default 30000+.
expectedOutput: You can reach nginx via NodePort and (if supported) LoadBalancer IP.
solutionCode:
# Edit Service type to NodePort
kubectl patch svc nginx-svc -p '{"spec":{"type":"NodePort"}}'
# For LoadBalancer with minikube:
minikube tunnel
# In another terminal:
kubectl patch svc nginx-svc -p '{"spec":{"type":"LoadBalancer"}}'
curl http://<EXTERNAL-IP>
